name: Casa Gaspar
key_features: White walled square closed to the outside; a higher central band opens to two courtyards with a pool.

name: Villa Busk
key_features: A 40 m concrete and timber wing on bedrock, linked by a glazed bridge to a four-storey tower with a pyramid roof.

name: Los Manantiales Restaurant
key_features: Four intersecting hyperbolic paraboloids form an eight-lobed concrete shell only centimetres thick.

name: Meiso no Mori Municipal Funeral Hall
key_features: Thin white concrete roof that rises and falls like a cloud, resting on tapered columns beside a pond.

name: Casa Rotonda
key_features: Three-level cylindrical house split north–south by a cut that brings daylight down from the roof.

name: Villa Schreiner
key_features: Low timber house on a modular grid, with Japanese-influenced post-and-beam structure and sliding walls.

name: Marie Short House
key_features: Two near-identical timber pavilions on stilts under curved corrugated metal roofs; louvres adjust air and light.

name: Hooper House II
key_features: Long fieldstone wall with an opening through its middle into a courtyard; glass faces the landscape behind.

name: Teatro Oficina
by: Lina Bo Bardi and Edson Elito
key_features: A long runway stage crosses a narrow lot under scaffold galleries, a glass side wall and an opening roof.

name: Sky House
key_features: A 10 x 10 m room raised on four wall-piers at the middle of each side, under a thin shell roof.

name: Hillside Terrace
key_features: Low mixed-use blocks built in phases along a street, with small courts and passages open to the sidewalk.

name: Casa Rustici
key_features: Two parallel slabs tied across the street front by thin balcony frames, leaving an open court between.

name: House in White
key_features: Square white house under a pyramidal roof, with a single cedar column standing in the main room.

name: Paper House
key_features: 110 paper tubes, 2.7 m tall, stand in an S-curve under a flat roof; the first building to use paper tubes as structure.

name: Fredensborg Houses
key_features: Courtyard houses strung along a slope, each with a walled garden, all facing a shared meadow.

name: Café De Unie
key_features: De Stijl facade of primary-coloured planes and lettering, rebuilt on a new site after its wartime loss.

name: Baker House
key_features: Serpentine brick dormitory gives every room an angled river view; stairs cascade down the rear facade.

name: Cocoa House
key_features: West Africa's first skyscraper, 26 storeys, built with cocoa-farming revenue as a symbol of the Western Region.

name: BedZED
key_features: Low-energy village: south-facing glazed terraces, roof gardens and bright wind cowls that ventilate the homes.

name: Crow Island School
by: Perkins, Wheeler & Will with Eliel and Eero Saarinen
key_features: One-storey wings off a shared core; every classroom has its own outdoor court, under a tall chimney tower.

name: Hubertus House
key_features: A rainbow-coloured steel and glass infill for single parents, stepping in among old street houses.

name: House N
key_features: Three boxes nested inside each other, each wall cut with big openings, so garden and house blur into layers.

name: Eames House
key_features: A Case Study House assembled from off-the-shelf industrial parts.

name: 25 bis rue Franklin
key_features: A concrete frame shown on the facade, filled with floral ceramic tiles, set around a U-shaped recessed front.

name: Eastgate Centre
key_features: Thermal mass and chimneys, modelled on termite mounds, cool offices without conventional air-conditioning.

name: Centro de Artes de Sines
key_features: Stone-clad blocks on both sides of a street, linked below ground; a glazed base opens to the pavement.

name: Jacobs II House (Solar Hemicycle)
key_features: A curved stone house bermed into earth on the north opens a glazed arc to a sunken south garden.

name: Spa Green Estate
key_features: Public housing with egg-crate concrete box-frame construction and aerodynamic wind-roofs.

name: Bilbao Metro entrances ("Fosteritos")
key_features: Curved glass shells that rise from the pavement over each metro stair, lit from within at night.

name: Collegio del Colle
key_features: Student rooms in brick-and-concrete terraces that step down the hillside facing Urbino.

name: Nantes School of Architecture
key_features: Concrete frame with extra-high floors linked by a ramp, leaving open unprogrammed spaces and a rooftop.

name: Mesa Laboratory (NCAR)
key_features: Clustered towers of bush-hammered concrete, tinted to match the Flatirons, sit on an open mesa top.

name: Diamond Ranch High School
key_features: Fragmented folded metal roofs either side of a long open-air street cut into a hillside.

name: Binoculars Building
by: Frank Gehry with Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen
key_features: Giant binoculars form the car entrance between a ship-like white wing and a copper tree-like wing.

name: Casa Gilardi
key_features: Indoor pool with a freestanding red column, lit through a yellow-glazed corridor.

name: Solar do Unhão
key_features: Colonial sugar estate turned museum, with a timber spiral stair joined like an ox cart.

name: Gando Primary School
key_features: Compressed-earth walls under a raised tin roof, built by the village.

name: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport Terminal 1
key_features: Round concrete drum crossed by glass-tube escalators, linked by tunnels to seven satellite gates.

name: Rabindra Bhavan
key_features: Home of three national arts academies: a Y-shaped four-storey block shaded by rows of concrete sunshades.

name: Salk Institute
key_features: Laboratories with service floors between them, around a travertine plaza open to the Pacific.

name: Church of Saint Francis of Assisi, Pampulha
key_features: A row of parabolic concrete vaults, with a painted tile mural covering the rear wall facing the lake.

name: Nuovo Villaggio Matteotti
key_features: Concrete housing designed with residents: terraced gardens and separate car and pedestrian paths linked by footbridges.

name: École de plein air de Suresnes
key_features: Open-air school against tuberculosis: eight classroom pavilions whose glazed walls fold open, on Mont-Valérien.

name: Michael Lee-Chin Crystal, Royal Ontario Museum
key_features: Five interlocking prisms of glass and aluminium burst out of the old museum's front onto Bloor Street.

name: Casa Luis Barragán
key_features: A blank wall to the street, and colour, light and gardens within.

name: CEPT University
key_features: An architecture school of brick and concrete, open to the campus at every level.

name: Bloomberg London
key_features: Two sandstone-framed blocks with bronze fins, split by a public arcade; the Roman Temple of Mithras is shown beneath.

name: Church on the Wind
key_features: A long frosted-glass colonnade leads to a concrete chapel framing a view of the hillside.

name: Bergpolderflat
by: Willem van Tijen, with Brinkman & Van der Vlugt
key_features: Nine-storey steel-framed slab with open access galleries: the first gallery-access high-rise flats in the Netherlands.

name: Quinta da Malagueira
key_features: About 1,200 white courtyard row houses, served by a raised concrete 'aqueduct' carrying water and power.

name: 30 Rockefeller Plaza
key_features: Slim limestone slab with stepped setbacks and vertical piers, centred on the plaza and rink.

name: Louvre-Lens
key_features: Low glass and brushed aluminium halls laid end to end on a former mine site, blurring into the park.

name: Reichstag
key_features: Glass dome with spiral ramps and a mirrored cone that reflects daylight into the chamber below.

name: Santa Maria da Feira Municipal Market
key_features: Butterfly-roofed concrete stalls stepping down a sloping site around an open courtyard.

name: Pousada Santa Maria do Bouro
key_features: A ruined monastery made into a hotel: the stone walls are kept, with flat new roofs and frameless glass set inside.

name: Central Saint Martins, Granary Building
key_features: An 1850s granary and its sheds turned into an art school, joined by a long top-lit internal street.

name: Commerzbank Tower
key_features: Triangular tower around a central atrium, with sky gardens spiralling up for natural ventilation.

name: Museum Frieder Burda
key_features: White panelled galleries with ramps and glass walls, bridged to the older Kunsthalle in a park.

name: Cité de la musique
key_features: Spiral internal street wraps an elliptical concert hall among fragmented volumes.

name: Diagoon Houses
key_features: Split-level 'unfinished' houses of two cores and half-floors that residents can enclose and extend.

name: University of Ruhuna
key_features: Pavilions with tiled roofs linked by covered walkways across hilltops overlooking the sea.

name: Casa O'Gorman 1929 (Cecil O'Gorman House)
key_features: Mexico's first functionalist house: a glazed studio box on pilotis with an outside spiral stair.

name: State Trading Corporation Building
key_features: Vierendeel trusses and Mughal-inspired polychrome sandstone cladding; Metabolist influence.

name: Braga Municipal Stadium
key_features: Two stands only, one carved from a granite quarry, linked by cables like an Inca rope bridge.

name: Casa Malaparte
key_features: Red masonry block on a cliff, with a wedge-shaped stair rising to a flat roof terrace and a curved white wall.

name: Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève
key_features: Upper-floor reading room with slender cast-iron columns carrying iron arches, left visible.

name: Minna no Mori Gifu Media Cosmos
key_features: An undulating cypress lattice roof with fabric globes that draw in daylight and exhaust warm air.

name: Cymbalista Synagogue
key_features: Twin towers square at the base and round at the top, one a synagogue and one a hall, lit from above.

name: Dominus Winery
key_features: Long low box walled in gabions of local basalt, which shade the cellars and let light filter through.

name: Breuer House II
key_features: Breuer's own timber house, cantilevered out from a smaller base, with a deck hung on steel cables.

name: Dutch Pavilion, Venice Biennale
key_features: A plain cubic gallery in the Giardini, lit by high clerestory windows in its raised centre.

name: East Hall of Foguang Temple
key_features: Seven-bay Tang timber hall with a hipped roof on deep bracket sets; Liang Sicheng found its date in 1937.

name: Gunma Music Center
key_features: Thin folded-plate concrete roof and walls zigzag over the hall, funded partly by citizens' donations.

name: Centre for Development Studies
key_features: Rat-trap bond and perforated brick jalis: cheap, cool and built by local masons.

name: Cosmic Rays Pavilion
key_features: Twin hyperbolic-paraboloid shells so thin they let cosmic rays through to the instruments.

name: Grady Gammage Memorial Auditorium
key_features: A round hall ringed by slender columns rising into arches, with long pedestrian bridges reaching out.

name: Vertical Courtyard Apartments
key_features: Housing towers with two-storey courtyards stacked into the facade, giving each flat a garden in the air.

name: Atelier Bardill
key_features: Red-brown concrete studio around a courtyard open to the sky through a large oval hole.

name: Cameron Offices
key_features: Office wings of precast post-tensioned concrete off an in-situ concrete mall, linked by a bridge over the avenue.

name: Naoshima Ferry Terminal
key_features: A thin flat roof on slender steel columns covers glass boxes and an open waiting space by the quay.

name: Robarts Library
key_features: Triangular-plan concrete stack tower with cantilevered upper floors over a broad podium.

name: Rovaniemi Library
key_features: Fan-shaped sunken reading areas lit by clerestories tuned to the low northern sun.

name: Teatro Colon
key_features: Horseshoe opera hall famed for its acoustics, with tiers of boxes under a painted dome.

name: Cathedral of Brasília
key_features: Sixteen curved concrete columns around a sunken, light-filled nave.

name: Supreme Court of Pakistan Building
key_features: Stepped white blocks with a deep colonnaded portico on Constitution Avenue; Neoclassical and Modernist blend.

name: Bacardi Bottling Plant
key_features: Roof of three square groined vaults, each two intersecting hyperbolic paraboloids, 4 cm thick at the edges.

name: Capilla del Retiro
key_features: Chapel set down into the ground below a lattice of laminated timber beams and glass, open to the Andes.

name: E-1027
key_features: Gray's white seaside house: pilotis, a long window band and ship-like balcony rails, with furniture she designed.

name: Casa Papanice
key_features: Curving walls and a ribbed facade of coloured ceramic-tube 'organ pipes' spread out from the corners.

name: Gartenstadt Falkenberg
key_features: Garden city terraces painted in strong colours, nicknamed the paintbox estate.

name: Paks Catholic Church
key_features: Timber-framed church with a shingled roof and three spires, its form drawn from Hungarian folk motifs.

name: Queen Elizabeth Hall
by: GLC Architects (Hubert Bennett, Jack Whittle, F. G. West, Geoffrey Horsefall)
key_features: Concert hall and Purcell Room in raw concrete, lifted on columns and laced with raised walkways on the South Bank.

name: Chemosphere (Malin Residence)
key_features: Octagonal house balanced on a single concrete column on a steep hillside, reached by a funicular.

name: Depot Boijmans van Beuningen
key_features: A bowl-shaped art store clad in mirror panels, with criss-crossing stairs in the atrium and a roof forest.

name: The Custom House
key_features: Four facades with coats of arms and sculpture by Edward Smyth; darker Irish limestone dome.

name: ATIRA (Ahmedabad Textile Industry's Research Association)
key_features: One of independent India's first modernist research campuses: a crisp framed lab block with long window bands.

name: Glass House, Seopjikoji
key_features: A V-shaped concrete-and-glass mass on the headland, opening east to Seongsan Ilchulbong.

name: Hedmark Museum
key_features: Concrete ramps and bridges thread through a medieval barn ruin under a new timber roof and glass.

name: Le Fresnoy
key_features: A great roof over the old 1920s leisure halls; the 'in-between' space under it holds catwalks and stairs.

name: Stegastein Viewpoint
key_features: A 30 m pine-and-steel walkway that leaps out from the hillside and stops in mid-air over the Aurlandsfjord.
